summary: End-to-end verification of the 5 security-hardening fixes (1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 3 LOW). Wrote and ran a new pytest file (test_security_fixes.py, 16 tests, all passing) covering SEC-001 connection-request approval flow, SEC-002 exercise-guide rate-limit exemption for cached lookups, CORS sanity, login/forgot-password rate limiting, and public certificate rate limiting. Also ran the FULL existing backend suite serially (-n 0) to avoid xdist worker DB races: 200 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped. Both failures are confirmed testing artifacts (external email-provider's OWN 429 rate limit exhausted from repeated pytest runs against the same coach account, and the forgot-password IP quota exhausted by my own preceding tests), NOT regressions introduced by the security fixes - verified via backend logs. Frontend: full manual Playwright walkthrough of both new UI flows - client Settings 'Connect to your coach' -> Email tab -> submit shows 'Request pending' card (not instant Connected); coach Clients tab shows 'Connection Requests' card with Approve/Deny buttons; clicking Approve on the correct row removed it from pending list and the client subsequently appeared in the coach's client list. Invite-code join re-verified instant (no approval step) via backend test. Cleaned up all throwaway TEST_ users/connection_requests created during testing.

minor.issue: Repeated automated test runs against the same coach email within a short window (my own test_security_fixes.py + pre-existing test_exercise_ai.py both call forgot-password for jcgfit@gmail.com) exhaust the 3/email or 8/IP-per-hour quota, causing an unrelated pre-existing regression test (test_exercise_ai.py::TestForgotPasswordRegression::test_forgot_password_no_500) to see a 429 instead of 202 when the full suite is run repeatedly back-to-back. Not a bug in the rate-limit logic itself (working as designed), just a testing-order side effect worth noting for CI - consider excluding real seeded accounts (jcgfit/ilovejeremygillespie) from repeated forgot-password test calls, or bump the per-email quota slightly, or use a dedicated throwaway account in that regression test.

test_phase7_booking.py::TestBookingReminders::test_reminder_sweep_sends_and_is_idempotent fails intermittently with email_sent=0 because the underlying Emergent email-sending provider itself returns its OWN 429 'email rate limit exceeded' (confirmed in backend logs), unrelated to any of the 5 security fixes (routes_booking.py was not touched in this pass). Pre-existing flakiness, not introduced by this change.

action_items: No code fixes required for the 5 security fixes themselves - all verified working correctly end-to-end.

Optional/low-priority: consider whether the two flaky pre-existing test failures noted above (forgot-password quota collision in CI, email-provider's own rate limit in booking reminders) warrant using dedicated throwaway test accounts instead of the real seeded jcgfit/ilovejeremygillespie accounts, to avoid future test-run collisions with the new rate limiters.
critical_code_review_comments: rate_limit.py is clean, small, and correctly separates 'count-every-attempt' (check_rate_limit) from 'count-only-failures' (check_rate_limit_failures_only + record_failed_attempt) - matches the stated login requirement precisely (successful logins never counted).

routes_misc.py accept_invite correctly differentiates coach-issued invite code (instant trust, connects immediately + auto-resolves any pending connection_requests to 'approved') from self-asserted coach_email (creates connection_requests doc, requires explicit coach approval) - this is the correct security boundary per SEC-001.

routes_coach.py connection-requests endpoints properly scope queries by coach_id ownership (approve/deny both filter on {'id': req_id, 'coach_id': user['user_id'], 'status': 'pending'}), preventing a coach from approving/denying another coach's requests.

routes_exercise_ai.py correctly rate-limits only the fresh-LLM-generation branch (after the cache-hit early return), exactly matching the SEC-002 requirement; confirmed empirically (6+ repeated calls to a cached exercise name never rate limited).

server.py CORS: allow_credentials=False with allow_origins=['*'] is the correct fix since Bearer-token auth never relied on cookies - verified no regression in login or Authorization-header-based calls.

success_rate.backend: 216/218 = 99% (200 pre-existing + 16 new security tests passed; 2 pre-existing failures are test-environment artifacts, not code regressions)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (both new UI flows - pending card and connection-requests approve - verified working)

seed_data_creation: Created and then cleaned up throwaway TEST_/test_secfix_/test_ui_client_ users and connection_requests docs used for the connection-request flow tests (via both pytest and Playwright). Did not modify jcgfit or ilovejeremygillespie real data except adding/approving one throwaway client's connection to jcgfit (harmless, coach now has one extra test client 'UI Test Client' - can be removed via DELETE /api/coach/clients/{id} if desired, not automatically cleaned up since removal requires coach auth).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 5 security fixes (SEC-001 connection-request approval, SEC-002 exercise-guide LLM rate limit, CORS credentials=False, login/forgot/reset rate limiting, certificate rate limiting) are verified working correctly on both backend and frontend. One residual cleanup item: coach jcgfit's client list now has one extra throwaway client 'UI Test Client' (test_ui_client_1788310151@test.com) from the Playwright approval test - safe to leave or remove via DELETE /api/coach/clients/{user_id} if a clean client list is needed for future demos. The two backend test failures found are pre-existing test-environment flakiness (external email provider's own rate limit, and test-run-order rate-limit quota collisions on the real coach account) and NOT regressions from this security pass.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no unresolved bugs found in the security fixes. The two full-suite-run failures are environmental/test-ordering artifacts (see backend_issues.minor) confirmed via backend logs showing the EXTERNAL email provider returning its own 429, and my own preceding rate-limit tests consuming the coach account's forgot-password quota before test_exercise_ai.py ran.
